scope: Experimental finite Split seam materialization; no native behavior or production GUI/MCP result observed.

control.observation: The Float32 midpoint rounds to [100000000, 4, 0], which is off the original edge. Both generated faces retain positive winding, so the collapse/winding check does not catch the area change.
control.representability: 100000000 and 100000008 are adjacent positive Float32 values; any interior point on this edge has an X strictly between them, so no exactly collinear Float32 interior point exists.

currentContract: Positions and IndexedMesh vertices support Float32Array or number arrays. The experimental precise candidate emits number arrays; default and production output remain Float32. indexedMeshMatches requires exact indexed and expanded coordinates.
precisionBoundaryControl: A number-array indexed mesh retains X=100000004 through the binary project codec and passes indexedMeshMatches. Actual scan display preparation chooses its indexed coordinates, but the Three.js Float32BufferAttribute used by the viewport rounds that value to 100000000. This is a codec/display-buffer/attribute control, not a rendered browser or public MCP test.
localOriginControl: For the same manufactured seam, subtracting [100000000,0,0] before creating a Float32BufferAttribute represents the midpoint as [4,4,0] and preserves the combined doubled triangle area of 192. This is arithmetic/attribute evidence only; no viewport rendering, object transform, selection, or picking behavior was tested.
localOriginRayControl: A synthetic translated Three.js mesh with local Float32 coordinates returns the same world-space hit with ordinary and indirect MeshBVH raycasting. This does not exercise the application viewport, picking worker, screen-selection path or GPU rendering.
workerAndPublicationBoundary: A mocked scan-edit result with aliased number-array positions and indexed vertices survives the actual worker dispatcher's structured-clone boundary with precision and alias retained. The GUI createSegments call previously omitted scan-edit indexed topology while MCP passed it to scanSegmentPublication; the local GUI handoff now passes the topology too. The GUI route has not been verified in a rendered application, and production Split does not yet emit the experimental topology.
candidatePublicationControl: The real experimental precise candidate ran for an interior-slit fixture via a mocked processing-client callback, then the shared mesh_process operation published the indexed result and binary project reopening retained positions and topology. The callback bypasses the worker and this is not a public MCP transport or GUI test.
candidateWorkerControl: The real experimental candidate ran via a substituted scan-edit callback in the actual worker dispatcher. The precise result survived structured cloning with indexed and expanded geometry matching. It does not connect the candidate to production, exercise browser workers, or establish native behavior.
preciseSeamPrototype: The opt-in precise seam output is connected to the experimental candidate and shared publication controls. Its allocation estimate excludes JavaScript engine overhead and is not a complete process-memory bound.
upstreamPrecisionGap: The precise candidate now propagates binary64 through edge contacts, face triangulation, assembly and seam materialization for the adjacent-Float32 control, preserving its midpoint, winding and area. Face binding prefers a unique exact edge parameter for distinct contacts that round to the same Float32 point; unresolved ambiguous bindings still reject. Other intermediate matching uses Float32 equivalence, so general precise behavior remains unverified.
preciseEdgeControl: The experimental precise edge-contact option preserves the midpoint across incident faces and distinct binary64 contacts that coincide in Float32; it is connected to the experimental candidate.

originalScanControl.scope: Manufactured covering triangle cutter on the original third PLY. Source hashes, total area and component count checked; this is not a native or rendered GUI/MCP comparison.

originalScanPartControl.scope: The precise seam was partitioned into two number-array parts. Each indexed mesh matched its expanded coordinates and the face counts summed to the seamed output; source hashes, total pre-partition area and group count also passed. Part-by-part geometric coverage, native output, browser and MCP were not verified.

originalScanCandidateControl.scope: Complete experimental candidate using a manufactured covering triangle cutter and retained indexed source. Source/cutter hashes, indexed-versus-expanded equality, aggregate area and one output part on each side of the cutter passed; no native, rendered GUI or public MCP behavior was tested.

limitations: The control does not prove native Split semantics or quantify distortion across real scans.
A 1e-6 relative face-coverage rejection also rejected an original-scan face and was removed; it is not a validated solution.
Higher-precision geometry or an alternative seam representation requires end-to-end assessment of rendering, topology, history, serialization, workers and public MCP.
The experimental finite Split path is not connected to production.

connectedPreciseCandidateOriginalScan.scope: Complete opt-in experimental candidate with binary64 refinement, manufactured covering cutter and original third PLY; source hashes, indexed equality, area and output sides checked. This is not native, rendered GUI or public MCP verification.

shortSegmentCollectorGap: The experimental precise collector retains the manufactured short interior segment and full candidate retains both referenced endpoints with positive winding and unchanged area. Near observations from opposite triangles use exact identity when available, while ambiguous cases without identity still reject. Coplanar matching, native behavior, actual GUI and public MCP remain unverified.
exactIntersectionIdentity: The precise collector now computes canonical rational identities lazily for close source-edge and cutter-edge observations. A shared one-third crossing with different binary64 rounding is reconciled with source-edge provenance; a distinct nearby crossing in the same Float32 cell remains distinct. A full candidate control preserves indexed equality, source winding and area. If exact identity is unavailable and rounded observations differ, the collector still rejects. Same-group and coplanar identity handling, native behavior and real GUI/public MCP remain unverified.
sameGroupPrecisionBoundary: For a manufactured axis-aligned source plane, two distinct exact crossings collapse to one binary64 point. The experimental collector restores constant plane coordinates to avoid a spurious off-plane difference, compares same-group canonical identities including exact vertices, and rejects the unrepresentable slit. The candidate test confirms source and cutter buffers stay unchanged. This does not establish correct rounding or rejection on arbitrary tilted planes, GUI/public MCP rollback or native equivalence.
tiltedRoundingAndRegistryGap: Exact rational coordinates now propagate through the experimental collector, shared-edge registry, face validation and assembly for noncoplanar edge crossings. The 64-case tilted-plane control and original ply-3 facet 740560 now pass, as does the full original scan. Coplanar-edge contact identity and arbitrary tilted geometry are not established; grouping, native behavior, rendered GUI and public MCP remain open.
exactRegistryCollision: A manufactured pair of different exact edge intersections shares one binary64 coordinate and nearby parameters. The former registry merged them when they had the same source identifier; the precise registry now compares exact identities and rejects this collision. A control confirms identical exact intersections with slightly different rounded parameters still merge. This is not native, rendered GUI or public MCP evidence.
coplanarSourceEdgeWitness: For a source edge lying in a noncoplanar cutter triangle plane, the precise collector can retain a verified cutter-edge/source-triangle crossing witness through registry, face and assembly. Sixty-four manufactured sloped-edge cases retain exact rounded coordinates, indexed-versus-expanded equality, positive winding and area; a two-neighbor control verifies propagation and rejects an inconsistent parameter. Entirely coplanar face overlap, arbitrary edge configurations, native equivalence, real GUI and public MCP remain unverified.
exactWitnessParameter: A witness crossing near a large-coordinate edge endpoint produced a different parameter when calculated from its rounded point. The experimental witness computes edge fraction and complement from exact rational coordinates, the collector retains them, and the registry rejects the incorrect rounded-point parameter. Controls cover reversed edges, a very small endpoint complement, source-edge provenance and the 64 sloped-edge cases. This does not prove entirely coplanar face handling or native and live GUI/public MCP behavior.
interiorContactRoundedToVertex: A manufactured cutter has exact interior source-edge contacts that round onto source vertices. The precise experimental collector compares exact identities and rejects the unrepresentable result, with a binary64-specific diagnostic; candidate source and cutter buffers remain unchanged. Genuine vertex contacts still pass. This does not exercise GUI/MCP error delivery or entirely coplanar faces.
productionPrecisionControl: The current shared finite-mesh Split route uses precise number-array coordinates, superseding the earlier currentContract and production-status descriptions above. A manufactured large-coordinate triangle and mesh cutter preserve x=100000004, positive signed doubled area 192, and unchanged input buffers in runScanEdit; m2-shared-large-precision-20261028-r1.json. A production-bundle browser replay found identical GUI/public-MCP output (five faces and two components), retained exact midpoint and area, source/cutter ownership, Undo/Redo and binary save/reopen, without page or console errors; m2-precision-browser-20261028-r1-guard.json. A follow-up on that same manufactured fixture aimed the camera at [100000002,8,0]: public viewport_pick returned that exact world point and a canvas click selected the source after selecting the cutter; m2-precision-canvas-20261028-r2-guard.json. This bounded picking control does not prove native behavior or arbitrary geometry and camera cases. The Float32-only helper still has a known expected failure. A strict collinearity rejection was tried and withdrawn because it rejected an existing real-scan face; m2-seam-float32-guard-20261028-r1.json records that failed attempt.
